requirements.closure_criteria: Establish one canonical gate state derived from executed evidence; all ledgers/contracts/config must consume that state rather than independently declaring closure.
requirements.finding: The repository carries mutually exclusive closure states. `.devtool.toml` says Gate D is reopened and OV15 blocked; `ov14_legacy_retirement_status.json` says Gate D is closed and OV15 ready; the product contract remains GateDQualified=false. A closed OV14 ledger therefore cannot be treated as canonical truth.
requirements.roadmap_reference: Original §2.2/§2.3, OV13 Gate D, OV14 required proof; amendment §2.2 and OV13 reconnect gate
requirements.title: Gate/ledger truth

requirements.closure_criteria: Make validators successor-aware and prove reachability/authority invariants rather than exact predecessor tokens or narrow symbol absence.
requirements.finding: Current validators disagree on the same tree. The retirement-truth validator reports no blockers/Gate-D-ready, REM03 reports Gate D still open with five blockers, REM05 reports Gate D closed/OV15 ready, while the historical OV14 validator requires the predecessor reopened state. The retirement validators also prove absence using narrow tokens instead of full production reachability.
requirements.roadmap_reference: Audit loop after every overlay; OV14 static/runtime retirement proof; gate evidence must be truthful
requirements.title: Audit machinery / retirement truth

requirements.closure_criteria: Retire/move the Python parity oracle out of production and make the compatible host command resolve to Go only after Gate D proof.
requirements.finding: The fresh snapshot still has a production Python/Textual host and package entry points.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV13 requires no production Python/Textual for supported host workflows; OV14 physically removes independent Python production backend
requirements.title: OV13/OV14 host retirement

requirements.closure_criteria: Prove CLI/TUI parity against frozen behavior fixtures with real commands and shared engine packages before claiming product-default.
requirements.finding: Fresh Go product metadata declares CLI/TUI product-default and seven supported workflows, but `main.go` exposes mostly contracts plus `scan`; there are no real query/search/activity/cleanup-review/cleanup-execute/diagnostics/export/tui host commands and `go/internal/tui/tui.go` has only Render/Smoke, not an interactive Run loop.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV13 requires real Go CLI + Go TUI for scan/query/search/status/activity/cleanup/diagnostics/evidence/machine-readable workflows using shared semantics
requirements.title: OV13 Go CLI/TUI parity

requirements.closure_criteria: Make stable semantic routes the actual production navigation identity and nest tools/reports under those routes; then remove the old shell.
requirements.finding: A six-route semantic contract exists, but production `DustUiApp` still navigates through the old `DustDestination`/`DustShellNavigation` model, including Certification, Deletion Reports/Cleanup, and Debug as direct destinations. UI/UX recheck: the WIP removes the 16-value shell, but the semantic hierarchy is still incomplete: SystemHome is the old Tools catch-all and entity/run/review/runtime/automation/settings routes and Android deep links are absent.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV13 new semantic route hierarchy product-default; OV14 removes old 16-destination/remapping shell and legacy top-level Debug/Certification/Deletion Reports routes
requirements.title: OV13/OV14 Android navigation cutover

requirements.closure_criteria: Route Android through typed Go product-authority operations; Kotlin should render/format already-authoritative models only.
requirements.finding: Production Android still computes domain policy locally through analyzers/engines for snapshots, residue, advanced analysis, package intelligence, recommendations, rules, growth, verification, duplicate projection, and module analysis.
requirements.roadmap_reference: Merged audit: Kotlin owns platform/presentation adapters only; OV09–OV13 retire Kotlin domain truth route-by-route
requirements.title: OV09–OV13 domain authority

requirements.closure_criteria: Keep product browsing/analysis paged or aggregate/bounded in Go and prevent UI/domain adapters from rebuilding a full-scan in-memory authority.
requirements.finding: The Android product path materializes whole scans and repeatedly runs list-level analysis. `GoDomainStore.entriesOnce()` drains every page; `MainViewModel` holds `allEntries`; `ScanRepository` repeatedly requests full entry lists for analysis/recommendations/rules/growth.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV04 requires paged/bounded query responses and million-scale bounded memory; RC-07 closes through OV04/OV05 and final scale qualification
requirements.title: OV04 bounded query / scale

requirements.closure_criteria: Expose domain operations through the Go runtime and bind Android adapters to them; prove stale-response/generation behavior and persistence.
requirements.finding: Go packages exist for these domains, but the Android runtime protocol does not expose the required product operations and Android does not consume them. The packages are therefore not yet the product authority.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV09 package/storage, OV10 intelligence, OV11 automation/activity, OV12 diagnostics/support become Go authorities; OV13 all supported Android flows use Go
requirements.title: OV09–OV12 Go runtime authority exposure

requirements.closure_criteria: Share the same scan semantics/implementation primitives between normal and privileged execution, keeping privilege transport as the only divergent layer.
requirements.finding: `go/internal/rootworker/scan.go` contains its own filesystem traversal/size/hardlink logic instead of reusing `go/internal/scan` authority.
requirements.roadmap_reference: Authoritative merged audit requires the same Go domain implementation in normal and privileged execution rather than a second scanner implementation
requirements.title: OV03/OV06 scan authority convergence

requirements.closure_criteria: Move duplicate verification semantics into the Go privileged/domain path and keep Kotlin as IPC/platform adapter.
requirements.finding: Exact duplicate verification remains in the Kotlin root service using SHA-256 edge/full hashing, while the Go privileged worker has no duplicate-verification command.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV10 duplicates migrate to Go; Kotlin must not retain domain verification policy
requirements.title: OV10 duplicate verification authority

requirements.closure_criteria: Make automation surfaces observe the same durable Go operation to terminal/recovery-required state before reporting terminal outcome.
requirements.finding: ScheduledScanWorker labels launch as non-terminal but still returns WorkManager Result.success immediately after launch; Tasker reports "accepted" immediately; there is no Android adapter consuming durable Go activity runs. UI/UX recheck: the WIP loads Go activityRuns into MainViewModel but DustUiApp never consumes them; ActivityList still renders CleanupReportsScreen, and there is no global active-operation/reconcile/recovery surface.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV11 request -> operationId -> observe durable operation -> report only terminal truth; WorkManager/Tasker/notifications/UI must share operation semantics
requirements.title: OV11 automation and Activity ownership

requirements.closure_criteria: Bind notification mutation/cancel actions to durable Go operation identity and replay-resistant admission metadata.
requirements.finding: Foreground notification cancellation is keyed by scan ID/action only and does not show a Go-issued nonce/expiry/single-use replay guard.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV11 notification surface shares durable operation ownership; cleanup/operation actions retain one-use/fail-closed safety semantics
requirements.title: OV11 notification cancellation capability

requirements.closure_criteria: Persist diagnostic truth in Go with bounded/redacted retention and have Android request sealed support evidence through Go.
requirements.finding: Go diagnostics contracts exist, but product diagnostics remain partly process-local Kotlin and support export is authored by Kotlin instead of a sealed Go support-evidence operation. UI/UX recheck: SystemDiagnostics still renders DebugWorkbenchScreen and Android does not present the Go ProblemGraph/root-cause/remediation model as the primary diagnostics experience.
requirements.roadmap_reference: OV12 requires durable Go diagnostics/evidence/privacy/retention/support bundle; canonical UX System > Diagnostics
requirements.title: OV12 diagnostics / support authority

requirements.closure_criteria: Move any retained migration fixtures to explicit archive-only location and remove production Room/NDJSON code/dependencies after proof of Go persistence/runtime parity.
requirements.finding: Fresh production still contains Room database/DAO/schema integration and NDJSON tail reader files. Even where runtime authority metadata says Room=false, physical retirement is incomplete.

## 6.3 Historical destinations absorbed by the new hierarchy

| Historical destination | Final home |
|---|---|
| `SCAN` | global Scan workflow |
| `EXPLORER` | Files → Explorer |
| `INSIGHTS` | Overview |
| `RECOMMENDATIONS` | Clean → Recommended |
| `RULES` | Clean → Rules |
| `GROWTH` | Overview → Trends |
| `LARGE_FILES` | Files → Large files |
| `DUPLICATES` | Clean → Duplicates |
| `APP_RESIDUE` | Clean → Residue, with contextual links from Apps |
| `SEARCH` | Files → Search |
| `PACKAGES` | Apps |
| `MODULES` | System → Modules |
| `CERTIFICATION` | System → Certification |
| `CLEANUP` / deletion reports | Activity → Run details |
| `DEBUG` | System → Diagnostics |
| `MORE` | removed as a semantic destination; replaced by explicit grouped routes |

This is a structural simplification: it preserves capabilities while removing navigation as an implementation inventory.

## 7.3 Landscape / large tablet

Prefer information-dense master/detail and persistent context rather than adding more navigation destinations.

The wide layout may reveal nested sections in the rail/drawer, but it must not turn every specialized workbench into a top-level peer again.

---

# 8. Route and stale-response safety

BKX's route-key/generation/response-binding idea should be adapted directly.

Each screen request binds to:

```text
routeKey
routeGeneration
entityKind
entityId
requestId
optional query/draft fingerprint
```

A late result is accepted only if all relevant identities still match.

For Dust this is especially important for:

- filesystem search while moving between directories;
- duplicate analysis while changing scan generation;
- residue analysis while package/user scope changes;
- app-storage details while changing package;
- cleanup review while candidates change;
- Activity detail while operation selection changes;
- diagnostics refresh while the underlying evidence generation advances.

The Go protocol should expose enough generation/revision information that this is not implemented as fragile Compose-local heuristics.

---

# 9. Shared screen-state contract

Every content route should expose one consistent presentation state:

```text
Loading
Empty(reason + primary recovery action)
Blocked(reason code + remediation)
Error(problem reference + retry/support action)
Content(data + freshness + action gates)
```

`Blocked` is intentionally distinct from Empty and Error because many DustUI states are valid-but-not-actionable:

- no trusted scan;
- stale after cleanup;
- wrong scan scope;
- root not available;
- scan incomplete/truncated;
- candidate evidence expired;
- cleanup capability already claimed;
- interrupted mutation requires reconciliation;
- package/storage evidence unsupported on this device/user.

This should replace screens that silently render zeroes/empty lists for insufficient evidence.

---

# 10. Visual language

Keep DustUI's existing modern dark/product language, but make it systematic.

## 10.3 Information density

DustUI should be denser than BKX where the domain demands it. File paths, storage statistics, scan evidence, and candidate comparisons benefit from compact rows and master/detail views.

The remodel should therefore borrow BKX's clarity, **not its exact spacing or card count**.

```text
  ↓
Preflight
  ├── root/runtime identity

Operation appears in Activity + global active-operation surface
  ↓
Completion
  ↓
Health evaluation
  ├── trusted/current → Overview/Files/Clean enabled
  └── degraded → visible problem + limited actions + remediation
```

## 11.4 Cleanup flow

Borrow BKX's strongest progressive-disclosure behavior and combine it with the new Go cleanup capability:

```text
Candidate discovery
  ↓
Inspect evidence
  ↓
Select candidates
  ↓
Build immutable manifest
  ↓
Review exact paths / bytes / reasons / fingerprints
  ↓
Explicit acknowledgement where required
  ↓
Claim single-use cleanup capability
  ↓
Execute
  ↓
Verify
  ↓
Activity run detail + refreshed/stale scan consequence
```

No recommendation card, duplicate row, residue row, file row, rule, notification, or automation bypasses this path.

## 11.9 System / Diagnostics

The old Debug Workbench becomes a user-comprehensible Diagnostics surface backed by XDM/XBS-style persistent evidence.

Primary view:

- top root causes from `DustProblemGraph`;
- current runtime/root health;
- scan health;
- evidence freshness;
- actionable remediation;
- support bundle action.

Advanced subsections can expose:

- structured event timeline;
- probes;
- protocol/runtime information;
- module scope evidence;
- raw operation correlation IDs.

Debugging detail remains available without making implementation internals a primary navigation destination.

---

# 12. Global operation UX

Operations must remain visible outside Activity without taking over every screen.

Use a compact global active-operation surface:

- top/hero card on Overview;
- small persistent progress surface/banner where appropriate;
- tap opens Activity run detail;
- cancel shown only when the Go action gate allows it;
- `Cancelling` is not presented as cancelled;
- lost transport is presented as `Reconnecting/Reconciling`, not failed or restarted automatically;
- interrupted/ambiguous mutations become `Recovery required`.

This directly connects BKX's activity clarity with chrootctl-style recovery semantics.

---

# 13. Action gating and disabled-state UX

Every risky or evidence-dependent action must receive a typed gate from the Go engine:

```text
allowed: bool
reasonCode: stable enum/string
message: plain-language explanation
remediationActions: optional typed actions
```

The UI never duplicates gate logic.

Examples:

- `SCAN_REQUIRED`
- `SCAN_STALE_AFTER_MUTATION`
- `SCAN_INTEGRITY_DEGRADED`
- `WRONG_SCOPE`
- `ROOT_UNAVAILABLE`
- `EVIDENCE_EXPIRED`
- `MANIFEST_CHANGED`
- `CAPABILITY_ALREADY_CLAIMED`
- `OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`
- `RECOVERY_REQUIRED`

Disabled buttons should expose the reason in context; important blocked workflows should show a notice with the remediation action rather than forcing users to discover why a button is disabled.

---

# 14. How the UI remodel changes the original bug-hunt fixes

The original findings remain acceptance requirements, but several UI fixes should no longer be implemented independently.
